summary.business: Lodha Developers Limited (formerly Macrotech Developers Limited) is an Indian real estate company built on three pillars: DevCo, its core residential development business across MMR, Pune, Bengaluru and (newly) NCR; RentCo, a growing annuity portfolio of industrial parks, high-street retail, select office assets and a powered-shell data-centre platform; and LandCo, a newly formalised vehicle to actively manage surplus land at its large Palava/Upper Thane holdings. It serves the top decile of India's households.

currentContext.strengths: India's most valuable real estate brand — ranked 59th most valuable brand in India overall by Kantar BrandZ, valued at US$2.2 Bn|Largest major-metro land holding of any developer in India — over 5,000 acres assembled at Palava and Upper Thane over two decades|Only Indian real estate company featured on Newsweek's World's Most Trustworthy Companies 2025 list|Credit rating of AA (Stable), reflecting seven rating upgrades since 2021|~H2,000 Bn of unsold GDV across planned, under-construction and ready inventory gives substantial growth visibility without significant new business-development investment|One of the first Indian developers to achieve carbon neutrality across Scope 1 and 2 emissions
currentContext.strategies: Four strategic pillars: (1) granular growth driven by superior talent and execution, (2) a 'super-market' approach to market expansion, (3) a phased, low-risk strategy for entry into new cities, (4) low-risk scale-up of annuity income streams.|'Super-market chain' model — developing strategically positioned, non-competing projects every 2-4 kilometres within core urban markets to reduce dependence on any single project or micro-market and capture meaningful long-term market share.|Each new city follows the same discipline: prove quality before scaling, and earn the right to grow.|Continue to invest only in opportunities that meet a 20%-plus RoE threshold while targeting DevCo becoming effectively debt-free within two to three years.|Strategy built on three complementary pillars anchored to the long India opportunity: DevCo (core residential development), RentCo (durable annuity income from industrial parks, retail, office and data-centre assets) and LandCo (active management/monetisation of surplus land at Palava and Upper Thane).|The Board has adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy (per Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations) that sets out the parameters and circumstances the Board considers in determining distribution of dividend to shareholders versus retaining profits. For FY26 the Board recommended a final dividend of H4.25 (42.5%) per equity share of face value H10, subject to shareholder approval, and did not transfer any amount to General Reserves during the year. The Company's stated balance-sheet discipline maintains net debt well below its stated internal leverage threshold, reflecting a policy of funding growth while limiting leverage rather than maximising near-term payout.
currentContext.expansion: The most distinctive capex/expansion initiative disclosed is a data-centre park being developed within the Palava township, with ~400 acres of shovel-ready land earmarked; the company plans to monetise roughly three-quarters of this land through outright sales to fund development of a 1 GW (gross power) built-to-suit (BTS) powered-shell platform to be leased to global data-centre operators on long-term leases (two global anchor operators already on site). Geographic expansion follows a phased playbook: a Pilot Phase lasting ~2 to 4 years focused on building a local team, understanding customer/regulatory nuances and executing one to two projects to establish sales and construction credibility, followed by a Growth Phase where the company scales across the city targeting ~15% market share. Over the past three years the company has reinforced its presence across MMR, Pune and Bengaluru; it is now scaling Bengaluru (moved from pilot to growth phase across four locations, with two more to start shortly) and, over the next 2-3 years, intends to launch pilot projects in the NCR to establish footprint and validate regional product-market fit.
currentContext.mdna: India's transition from a low-income to a middle-income economy, with rising household incomes and increased discretionary spending, is expected to provide a sustained long-term growth runway for residential, commercial and mixed-use real estate.|A clear shift in buyer preference toward branded/tier-1 developers is underway, with execution capability, timely delivery and project quality emerging as primary market differentiators, concentrating market share among established developers.|Despite muted launches in CY25 vs CY24, total value of housing sales in the top-7 cities rose (Anarock), reflecting strong absorption; premiumisation trend continues as developers pivot away from the affordable segment amid constrained supply there.|Recent easing of interest rates is expected to catalyse a gradual recovery in affordable and mid-income housing segments; CY26 is expected to be a constructive year for residential real estate with resilient demand across all product segments.|MMR is India's largest housing market (30.1% of new launches, 32.3% of absorption in top-7 cities in CY25); large infrastructure pipeline (Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link, Coastal Road, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Metro expansion, Airoli-Palava freeway, bullet train) seen as a multi-decade tailwind for MMR per-capita income and real estate.|Pune market showed balanced demand-supply (inventory overhang down to 15 months from a 48-month CY20 peak), underpinned by a diversified employment base (IT, automotive, manufacturing, engineering, defence, and growing GCC presence) with a structural pivot toward higher-priced housing.|Bengaluru housing demand supported by GCC-driven office space growth and a structural shift toward larger, amenity-rich premium homes; inventory overhang lean at 13 months.|NCR has seen inventory overhang fall sharply from 88 months (CY20) to 19 months (CY25), with demand consolidating toward tier-1 developers and premium/luxury housing even as near-term volumes and prices may moderate against a high base.|Management views Indian housing demand as structural rather than cyclical, unlike globally cyclical housing markets, given under-penetration of real estate in India's GDP (~7% vs 13-15% in developed economies, 21% in China) and rising per-capita income (from US$2,000 toward US$5,000 over the decade) expanding the homeownership-capable household base from ~77 Mn toward ~175 Mn.|Structural reforms (RERA, demonetisation, GST) and tighter lending norms have addressed past supply-side excesses, fostering a disciplined and transparent housing market.|H2,000 Bn of unsold GDV across planned, under-construction and ready inventory, giving substantial growth visibility without significant new business-development investment.|Added 12 new projects during FY26 with an aggregate Gross Development Value (GDV) of ~H600 Bn — 2.4x the annual guidance.|Operations span nearly 40 locations across MMR, Pune and Bengaluru, with plans to start operations in the NCR market in FY27; entered NCR through two capital-light joint development agreements.|Operational footprint expanded into eight new locations during FY26; key launches included Lodha Alibaug, Lodha Elan, Lodha Aureus and Lodha Sovrano in MMR, Lodha Heaven and Lodha Elanza in Bengaluru, and Lodha Camelot and Lodha Sylvan in Pune.|Delivered ~6,373 homes during FY26; management anticipates a significant acceleration in deliveries during FY27 as construction scales across the portfolio.|Bengaluru has moved from pilot to growth phase across four locations, with two more locations to start shortly.

risks.note: Increasing frequency and intensity of floods and extreme heat events pose risks of property damage, construction delays, operational disruptions, reduced workforce productivity, and heightened health and safety hazards across project sites and operational assets.
Managing lifecycle Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions amid structural market shifts towards green buildings and evolving regulatory transition requirements creates cost and compliance exposure.

High freshwater dependence, inadequate recycling, and inefficient infrastructure risk supply shortages, rising operational costs, regulatory non-compliance, and reputational risk, particularly during water-stressed periods.

Health and safety lapses risk workplace injuries, fatalities, legal liabilities, construction delays, and reputational damage, while undermining workforce morale, contractor productivity, and execution efficiency.

risks.risk: Human rights and labour management risk
risks.note: Inadequate human rights protection, unfair labour practices, or unsafe working conditions risk regulatory non-compliance, reduced productivity, workforce dissatisfaction, attrition, and reputational damage, threatening long-term business continuity.

risks.risk: Business ethics, transparency and governance risk
risks.note: Weak governance, ethical lapses, or a lack of transparency risk regulatory penalties, diminished investor confidence, reputational damage, and erosion of stakeholder trust.

one-line thesis: Lodha delivered record Q3 presales (INR 56bn, +25% YoY) driven by brand consolidation in premium segments and successfully pivoted its massive Palava land bank into a high-value AI data center hub with anchor tenants (AWS, STT), creating a dual-engine growth model of residential sales and long-term annuity income. While collections dipped due to lumpy prior-year land sales and temporary environmental clearance delays, the resolution of these bottlenecks and the expansion into NCR position the company for accelerated cash flow generation and margin expansion over the next 18 months.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 46.6bn (+29% YoY); Adjusted EBITDA: INR 14.9bn (+23% YoY), Margin ~32%; PAT: INR 9.5bn (Pro forma ~INR 12bn, ~21% margin); Order Book (Presales): INR 56bn in Q3 (Record), INR 146bn for 9MFY26 (70% of guidance); Net Debt: INR 61.7bn (0.28x Equity). One-offs/Distortions: Collections down 17% YoY due to significant land sale proceeds in Q3FY25 base and construction delays from environmental clearances now resolved; No lumpy land sales confirmed for Q3FY26.
guidance: Presales: INR 210bn for FY26 (On track); Embedded EBITDA Margin: ~33% for FY26; Order Inflow: Strong launch pipeline of INR 120bn+ in Q4; Capex/Commissioning: Data center construction to begin post-client specification finalization (BTS model); OCF Guidance revised to ~INR 70bn (+/- 5%) from INR 77bn due to construction delays.
order book & pipeline: 9M FY26 presales at INR 146bn (70% of full year target); Q3 single quarter record at INR 56bn (+25% YoY); Business Development added INR 340bn GDV in Q3 (Total ~INR 600bn added in 9 months); Pipeline of developable projects next 5 years > INR 2 lakh crores.
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: 80% of home sales by value across Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore, and new NCR entry (2 pilot projects, INR 33bn GDV); Price growth 4% YTD, targeting 5-6% for FY26. Townships: Palava & Upper Thane (4,000 acres) seeing infrastructure completion (Freeway, Highway, Airport, Bullet Train) driving premiumisation (targeting 50% sales from premium segment by decade end vs 20% in FY25). Data Centers: 400 acres earmarked, 3GW power allocated, 2 anchor clients (AWS, STT) signed; Land value expected to rise from INR 21cr/acre to INR 50-60cr/acre over 3 years.
growth verticals / optionality: NCR expansion following Bangalore playbook (Pilot -> Growth phase); Palava Data Center park scaling to INR 1.3 lakh crore total investment (Lodha + clients); Build-to-suit powered shells generating long-term rental annuity; Premiumisation of township mix driving margin expansion; Consolidation of land bank opportunities as market froth cools.
margins & cost dynamics: Embedded EBITDA margin ~32% in Q3 despite low land sales contribution; FY26 guidance ~33%; Construction costs stable (steel/cement reasonable); Commodity price hikes (copper/silver) have <1% impact on cost base; Significant contingencies in budget often result in margin upside.
capex / expansion: Data Center turnkey capex reduced to ~$6mn/MW (vs global $8-12mn) due to Green DC policy benefits; Power shell construction cost ~INR 3cr/MW including land; Residential construction spend ~INR 30bn for 9M (below desired levels due to delays), expected to ramp to ~INR 12bn in Q4.
capital allocation: Disciplined net debt target <0.5x equity (currently 0.28x); Front-loaded business development in FY26 to be moderated in next 24 months to focus on profitability and balance sheet strengthening; Cash generation to improve as construction accelerates and collections pick up.
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on construction ramp-up post-environmental clearances; Potential moderation in industry volumes (entry-level segment decline); Uncertainty on timing of future lumpy land sales; Dependency on infrastructure completion timelines for township value uplift; Regulatory changes in data center policies.
management quality / tone: Confident and constructive; Emphasizes brand strength, execution capability, and disciplined underwriting; Highlighted resolution of operational bottlenecks; Strategic shift towards high-margin annuity assets (data centers) while maintaining residential leadership.
non-obvious takeaways: The data center park's competitive moat lies not just in land but in unique infrastructure: 3GW power from 5 circuits (Tier 4 reliability), 100M liters of non-potable water for cooling, and 5+ fiber routes; This allows clients to reduce opex by 30% and capex by 15%, making Palava globally competitive ($0.06/kWh power cost vs $0.10-0.12 in US); The 'premiumisation' of Palava is structurally supported by imminent connectivity upgrades (Bullet Train to BKC in <20 mins, New Navi Mumbai Airport) rather than just cyclical demand.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for reliable, low-cost, green power and water for AI workloads | AWS India | beneficiary | High | Anchor tenant securing cost-advantaged infrastructure ($6mn/MW capex, $0.06/kWh power) in Mumbai region. |
| Requirement for scalable, compliant data center capacity in financial hub | STT GDC India | beneficiary | High | Temasek subsidiary leveraging Lodha's regulatory approvals and utility infrastructure for expansion. |
| Supply chain constraints and labor availability in booming real estate market | Lodha's Vendor Partners | beneficiary | Med | Management emphasized strong relationships and fair wage practices to ensure continuity, benefiting aligned contractors. |
| Oversupply in mid-income segments and declining volumes in affordable housing | Unorganized/Small Real Estate Developers | loser | High | Market consolidating towards branded players; entry-level segment (<INR 75L) seeing volume decline, hurting non-branded supply. |

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

segment_detail.body: Residential: 80% of home sales by value across Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore, and new NCR entry (2 pilot projects, INR 33bn GDV); Price growth 4% YTD, targeting 5-6% for FY26. Townships: Palava & Upper Thane (4,000 acres) seeing infrastructure completion (Freeway, Highway, Airport, Bullet Train) driving premiumisation (targeting 50% sales from premium segment by decade end vs 20% in FY25). Data Centers: 400 acres earmarked, 3GW power allocated, 2 anchor clients (AWS, STT) signed; Land value expected to rise from INR 21cr/acre to INR 50-60cr/acre over 3 years.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: 9M FY26 presales at INR 146bn (70% of full year target); Q3 single quarter record at INR 56bn (+25% YoY); Business Development added INR 340bn GDV in Q3 (Total ~INR 600bn added in 9 months); Pipeline of developable projects next 5 years > INR 2 lakh crores.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Presales: INR 210bn for FY26 (On track); Embedded EBITDA Margin: ~33% for FY26; Order Inflow: Strong launch pipeline of INR 120bn+ in Q4; Capex/Commissioning: Data center construction to begin post-client specification finalization (BTS model); OCF Guidance revised to ~INR 70bn (+/- 5%) from INR 77bn due to construction delays.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: NCR expansion following Bangalore playbook (Pilot -> Growth phase); Palava Data Center park scaling to INR 1.3 lakh crore total investment (Lodha + clients); Build-to-suit powered shells generating long-term rental annuity; Premiumisation of township mix driving margin expansion; Consolidation of land bank opportunities as market froth cools.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's transition from a low-income to a middle-income economy, with rising household incomes and increased discretionary spending, is expected to provide a sustained long-term growth runway for residential, commercial and mixed-use real estate.
- A clear shift in buyer preference toward branded/tier-1 developers is underway, with execution capability, timely delivery and project quality emerging as primary market differentiators, concentrating market share among established developers.
- Despite muted launches in CY25 vs CY24, total value of housing sales in the top-7 cities rose (Anarock), reflecting strong absorption; premiumisation trend continues as developers pivot away from the affordable segment amid constrained supply there.
- Recent easing of interest rates is expected to catalyse a gradual recovery in affordable and mid-income housing segments; CY26 is expected to be a constructive year for residential real estate with resilient demand across all product segments.
- MMR is India's largest housing market (30.1% of new launches, 32.3% of absorption in top-7 cities in CY25); large infrastructure pipeline (Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link, Coastal Road, Navi Mumbai International Airport, Metro expansion, Airoli-Palava freeway, bullet train) seen as a multi-decade tailwind for MMR per-capita income and real estate.
- Pune market showed balanced demand-supply (inventory overhang down to 15 months from a 48-month CY20 peak), underpinned by a diversified employment base (IT, automotive, manufacturing, engineering, defence, and growing GCC presence) with a structural pivot toward higher-priced housing.
- Bengaluru housing demand supported by GCC-driven office space growth and a structural shift toward larger, amenity-rich premium homes; inventory overhang lean at 13 months.
- NCR has seen inventory overhang fall sharply from 88 months (CY20) to 19 months (CY25), with demand consolidating toward tier-1 developers and premium/luxury housing even as near-term volumes and prices may moderate against a high base.
- Management views Indian housing demand as structural rather than cyclical, unlike globally cyclical housing markets, given under-penetration of real estate in India's GDP (~7% vs 13-15% in developed economies, 21% in China) and rising per-capita income (from US$2,000 toward US$5,000 over the decade) expanding the homeownership-capable household base from ~77 Mn toward ~175 Mn.
- Structural reforms (RERA, demonetisation, GST) and tighter lending norms have addressed past supply-side excesses, fostering a disciplined and transparent housing market.
- H2,000 Bn of unsold GDV across planned, under-construction and ready inventory, giving substantial growth visibility without significant new business-development investment.
- Added 12 new projects during FY26 with an aggregate Gross Development Value (GDV) of ~H600 Bn — 2.4x the annual guidance.
- Operations span nearly 40 locations across MMR, Pune and Bengaluru, with plans to start operations in the NCR market in FY27; entered NCR through two capital-light joint development agreements.
- Operational footprint expanded into eight new locations during FY26; key launches included Lodha Alibaug, Lodha Elan, Lodha Aureus and Lodha Sovrano in MMR, Lodha Heaven and Lodha Elanza in Bengaluru, and Lodha Camelot and Lodha Sylvan in Pune.
- Delivered ~6,373 homes during FY26; management anticipates a significant acceleration in deliveries during FY27 as construction scales across the portfolio.
- Bengaluru has moved from pilot to growth phase across four locations, with two more locations to start shortly.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Embedded EBITDA margin ~32% in Q3 despite low land sales contribution; FY26 guidance ~33%; Construction costs stable (steel/cement reasonable); Commodity price hikes (copper/silver) have <1% impact on cost base; Significant contingencies in budget often result in margin upside.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Disciplined net debt target <0.5x equity (currently 0.28x); Front-loaded business development in FY26 to be moderated in next 24 months to focus on profitability and balance sheet strengthening; Cash generation to improve as construction accelerates and collections pick up.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The most distinctive capex/expansion initiative disclosed is a data-centre park being developed within the Palava township, with ~400 acres of shovel-ready land earmarked; the company plans to monetise roughly three-quarters of this land through outright sales to fund development of a 1 GW (gross power) built-to-suit (BTS) powered-shell platform to be leased to global data-centre operators on long-term leases (two global anchor operators already on site). Geographic expansion follows a phased playbook: a Pilot Phase lasting ~2 to 4 years focused on building a local team, understanding customer/regulatory nuances and executing one to two projects to establish sales and construction credibility, followed by a Growth Phase where the company scales across the city targeting ~15% market share. Over the past three years the company has reinforced its presence across MMR, Pune and Bengaluru; it is now scaling Bengaluru (moved from pilot to growth phase across four locations, with two more to start shortly) and, over the next 2-3 years, intends to launch pilot projects in the NCR to establish footprint and validate regional product-market fit.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and constructive; Emphasizes brand strength, execution capability, and disciplined underwriting; Highlighted resolution of operational bottlenecks; Strategic shift towards high-margin annuity assets (data centers) while maintaining residential leadership.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- India's most valuable real estate brand — ranked 59th most valuable brand in India overall by Kantar BrandZ, valued at US$2.2 Bn
- Largest major-metro land holding of any developer in India — over 5,000 acres assembled at Palava and Upper Thane over two decades
- Only Indian real estate company featured on Newsweek's World's Most Trustworthy Companies 2025 list
- Credit rating of AA (Stable), reflecting seven rating upgrades since 2021
- ~H2,000 Bn of unsold GDV across planned, under-construction and ready inventory gives substantial growth visibility without significant new business-development investment
- One of the first Indian developers to achieve carbon neutrality across Scope 1 and 2 emissions

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on construction ramp-up post-environmental clearances; Potential moderation in industry volumes (entry-level segment decline); Uncertainty on timing of future lumpy land sales; Dependency on infrastructure completion timelines for township value uplift; Regulatory changes in data center policies.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The data center park's competitive moat lies not just in land but in unique infrastructure: 3GW power from 5 circuits (Tier 4 reliability), 100M liters of non-potable water for cooling, and 5+ fiber routes; This allows clients to reduce opex by 30% and capex by 15%, making Palava globally competitive ($0.06/kWh power cost vs $0.10-0.12 in US); The 'premiumisation' of Palava is structurally supported by imminent connectivity upgrades (Bullet Train to BKC in <20 mins, New Navi Mumbai Airport) rather than just cyclical demand.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Four strategic pillars: (1) granular growth driven by superior talent and execution, (2) a 'super-market' approach to market expansion, (3) a phased, low-risk strategy for entry into new cities, (4) low-risk scale-up of annuity income streams.
- 'Super-market chain' model — developing strategically positioned, non-competing projects every 2-4 kilometres within core urban markets to reduce dependence on any single project or micro-market and capture meaningful long-term market share.
- Each new city follows the same discipline: prove quality before scaling, and earn the right to grow.
- Continue to …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for reliable, low-cost, green power and water for AI workloads | AWS India | beneficiary | High | Anchor tenant securing cost-advantaged infrastructure ($6mn/MW capex, $0.06/kWh power) in Mumbai region. |
| Requirement for scalable, compliant data center capacity in financial hub | STT GDC India | beneficiary | High | Temasek subsidiary leveraging Lodha's regulatory approvals and utility infrastructure for expansion. |
| Supply chain constraints and labor availability in booming real estate market | Lodha's Vendor Partners | beneficiary | Med | Management emphasized strong relationships and fair wage practices to ensure continuity, benefiting aligned contractors. |
| Oversupply in mid-income segments and declining volumes in affordable housing | Unorganized/Small Real Estate Developers | loser | High | Market consolidating towards branded players; entry-level segment (<INR 75L) seeing volume decline, hurting non-branded supply. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate identity] The company was formerly known as Macrotech Developers Limited and now reports as Lodha Developers Limited.
- [Government MOUs] Signed two MOUs with the Maharashtra government to invest and facilitate INR 130,000 crore (~US$14bn) in its DC Park, which is approved under the state's Green Integrated Data Centre Park Policy carrying significant fiscal incentives for operators.
- [Anchor tenants] AWS, ST Telemedia (Temasek-backed) and Digital Edge have all bought into the DC Park; the Jun-26 Digital Edge transaction at ~INR 425mn/acre was roughly double the CY25 price of ~INR 210mn/acre, a 16x land value uplift in about five years.
- [Philanthropy] Lodha Foundation launched the Lodha Theoretical Physics Institute, India's first privately funded institution of its kind under Wolf Prize winner Prof. Jainendra Jain, alongside a planned Mathematical Sciences Institute under Fields Medallist Manjul Bhargava.
- [Leadership depth] Senior team is largely lateral hires from DLF, Godrej Properties, Brigade, Adani, McKinsey and JSW, with market-level CEOs for Mumbai Suburbs, Pune, Bengaluru, NCR and Retail & Offices.
